rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically complete but the $40M favorable-to-unfavorable run-off reversal is structurally responsible for ~30% of the GAAP loss vs prior year, and management does not foreground that this is mean-reversion of a 2024 benefit rather than a new structural deterioration. Moderate (not severe) because the data IS in the filing.

rfm_tuples.R: We currently believe that our cash on hand, marketable securities, cash flows from operations, and availability under the Facility will be adequate to meet our liquidity requirements for 2026. ... we had outstanding letters of credit and borrowings totaling $370 million under the [revised $750M] Facility. ... rfm_tuples.f: Going-concern / covenant-stress check — going_concern_local + sec_filings: does the issuer disclose covenant amendments needed to remain compliant? Is this a Mode B red flag (dividend was carved out, leverage cap raised — i.e., they would have breached without the amendment)?

This is an admission that under the original covenant package they would have been at-risk. However: (i) they were in compliance at 3/31/2026, (ii) net debt is modest ($370M drawn vs $660M cash, though much of that cash is restricted client-payroll funds), (iii) Facility matures Dec 15, 2028 — 2.5 years runway, (iv) dividend was maintained at $0.60/qtr throughout 2025. No going-concern qualification from EY (auditor since 1991).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Covenant relief was disclosed but framed neutrally; reader must connect that NSP needed accommodation. Not severe — runway is real and no going-concern flag — but liquidity stress is more visible than the upbeat framing suggests.

supplemental_signals.honesty_alpha_assessment: NSP is the inverse of a typical Signal-OS short candidate. The disclosure is honest (no concealed deterioration), the auditor is long-tenured and clean, the dividend is maintained, the credit facility is amended-but-compliant with 2.5y runway, and the most informed insiders are deploying meaningful personal capital ($8.4M aggregate, $7.5M by the CEO alone) at the drawdown lows. The -47.5% drawdown reflects a real but disclosed 2025 earnings collapse driven by medical-cost inflation and an unfavorable claims-run-off reversal — both of which are mean-reverting cyclical PEO-industry headwinds rather than structural impairment. Per the honesty-alpha framework, NSP fails the SHORT criteria (no concealment) and meets the LONG criteria (insider buying + honest disclosure + cyclical-not-structural impairment).

summary: NSP disclosed its FY2025 collapse (net income -108%, Adj EBITDA -51%) honestly and prominently in the 10-K MD&A. Q1 2026 (10-Q filed 2026-05-01) shows sequential stabilization (Adj EBITDA +1% YoY, net income $33M positive). The decisive signal is Form 4: CEO Paul Sarvadi made open-market PURCHASES (code P) totaling ~$7.56M / 301,987 shares in March and May 2026, with CFO Allison ($205k), General Counsel Callens, and Director Masterson also buying in March 2026 — all in post-disclosure blackout-open windows, none under 10b5-1 plans. Aggregate executive/director open-market buys Aug 2025-May 2026: $8.4M. CEO buy:sell dollar ratio: 13:1. Auditor EY (since 1991) clean, dividend maintained at $0.60/qtr, credit facility 2.5y runway with covenant compliance. Mild flags only: covenant amendment, capitalized HR Scale dev costs, $40M claims-run-off swing. VERDICT: LONG-tier. This is exactly the inverse of a short candidate — honest disclosure + insider conviction into priced-in cyclical impairment.
